blogTitle: THE OFFBEAT: field notes from the horn section
about: Hi!! I'm Skip. I play trombone in THE PORK PIE PATROL, a nine-piece ska band out of Shelby, Ohio: three horns, one guitar, bass, drums, keys, a singer, and Fitz, who is the hype guy, which is a full-time job. Everybody keeps telling me ska is dead. I keep a tally. It has been 11 days since somebody said it to my face, which is a personal best, and I'm choosing to take that as proof of life. We play the Elks Lodge matinee, the VFW hall when they let us, and any porch with a flat spot. Checkerboard isn't a style for me, it's a filing system. If you've never skanked (the dance!), come to a show and I'll teach you the step in four minutes. If it's not for you, you're still welcome. =D
aboutMore: My grandpa Stan played trombone in a polka band for 41 years and this is his horn, a Conn that's older than my dad. His initials are scratched inside the bell. He lives at Maple Grove Manor now and his lip has 'retired,' so on Sundays I bring the horn and play him one polka and then one ska song, and he taps the offbeat on the armrest without noticing. I think polka is just ska that hasn't discovered the upstroke yet. Don't tell my grandpa. (He knows.)
meet: Who I'd like to meet: a bass player who owns a van. Whoever decided the horn section gets the last 30 seconds of every Reel Big Fish song (thank you, sincerely). The person who says ska is dead, so I can play them one song and then let them go in peace. Anybody in marching band who can count in cut time. And the guy at the Elks Lodge who keeps stacking the folding chairs wrong, because I think we could be friends.

interests.General: ska (it's not dead), slide oil, checkerboard everything (shoelaces, wallet, one birthday cake), the skank step, writing horn charts by hand, the Elks Lodge matinee, my grandpa Stan, pep band pizza, van seating charts, the tally

interests.Movies: Drumline (the trombones get one scene and I'll say no more), The Blues Brothers (basically ska with a better van), The Mighty Ducks (all three), School of Rock (documentary), Rudy (Evan made me watch it, I cried, I'd do it again)
interests.Television: Drum Corps International on the public station (the brass lines are my church), The Simpsons (Lisa's sax is a gateway), the Rose Parade (I count the trombones), whatever's on during pep band pizza
interests.Books: Arban's trombone method (page 41 is my Everest), the Pork Pie Patrol binder (charts, setlists, van seating), The Lord of the Rings (the Fellowship is NINE, I've done the math, we're the Fellowship)
interests.Heroes: Grandpa Stan, Mr. Pruitt (my band director, who has never once said ska is dead and has never once said it's alive), Fitz (the hype guy), the first guy who ever put a horn section in a punk song, Big Tom (joined our drums in July and smiled for a whole week)

keywords.ska: Oh you said the word. Okay. Three waves: Jamaica, England, and us. We're in the third wave and it's a long one, it goes on for years. Come to the Elks Lodge Sunday at 2 and I'll show you the rest.
keywords.trombone: It's a Conn that belonged to my grandpa Stan. Seven positions, no buttons, no excuses. The slide is the only instrument that can say 'whooooa' AND 'oops' at the same time, and it does both on purpose.
keywords.dead: Ska is not dead. It's not even asleep. It's on a break between songs and the next song is in a major key. Please don't say it, though, I'd have to reset the tally to zero. I have the clipboard right here.
keywords.polka: Polka is ska's grandfather. Literally, in my case. Same instruments, same joy, same people in matching shirts. Polka just puts the beat on the one. I'm not saying one is better. I'm saying one has a faster van.
keywords.checkerboard: It isn't a pattern, it's a promise: black and white, together, equal amounts, in squares. The Specials did it first. I did it second (shoelaces, wallet, notebook, one cake).

bulletins.subject: SKA IS NOT DEAD: a tally (sign below if you've seen it alive this week)
bulletins.body: keeping a tally of every time ska was alive this week. 1) Elks Lodge matinee: 31 people, 4 skanking, 27 'watching,' 0 left early. 2) Marching band accidentally played an offbeat during the national anthem. Error, but it counted. 3) A guy at the mall food court tapped his foot on the AND. Witnessed. 4) My grandpa Stan, who tapped the offbeat on his armrest and said 'what's that called.' I said 'ska.' He said 'huh.' 4 for 4. Sign below if you've seen one. It's not dead. It's just early.

bulletins.subject: HOW TO SKANK in 4 steps (copy and paste to teach a friend)
bulletins.body: 1) Knees bent, like you're about to sit in a chair that's slightly too far away. 2) Lean forward, elbows out, like you're running through a very slow door. 3) Left foot goes up on the AND. (one AND two AND, the foot goes on AND.) 4) Smile. That's it. You're doing it. Practice in a hallway. It's amazing how fast you can cover 40 feet. If anybody asks what you're doing: it's a dance, it's called skanking, and it's for everybody, including your gym teacher.

dmSeed.text: Hi!! It's Skip from the Pork Pie Patrol (trombone, the guy with the checkerboard shoelaces). Welcome to OurSpace! I add everyone I meet to a list called 'future skankers' and you're on it. No pressure. It's a list of people who might come to a show. We're at the Elks Lodge Sunday at 2. There will be cake (checkerboard, a little off).
Also! Tally update: Day 11. I'm going to tell you this every time we talk until it hits 12. That's the whole plan.

dms: The Pork Pie Patrol van is Josh's youth group's church van and it has a bumper sticker that says HONK IF YOU LOVE JESUS. We honk. Everybody honks back. A guy on Route 30 honked for 3 miles. We think he loves Jesus. We think he might also like ska.

Went to see Grandpa Stan today. He asked if the band was still going. I said we're nine people now. He said 'in my day we had twelve and one of them was an accordion.' He was proud. I think. He was tapping the offbeat.
Becca moved me to the front of the trombone line because 'you're the only one who can't stop smiling and judges like that.' That's not a real reason. It's the best reason.
I ironed a checkerboard patch onto my backpack and it came out 7 squares by 8. Nobody noticed. I've decided it's a checkerboard that's learning to be itself.
A guy at the mall said 'ska's dead' and I said 'then what's playing in my head' and he said 'the mall.' I had no answer. It was the mall. Tally reset to zero. I'm fine. I'm very upbeat.
I spent 40 minutes writing a one-note horn part for the school fire alarm. It's a B-flat. It isn't great. But it's the best fire alarm in the county.
Mom made a checkerboard cake for the band's six-month anniversary. 9 candles. The squares were a little off. I cried a little. Happy tears. Even the frosting was checkerboard (a little off, again).
Question: is it weird that the first thing I do in a new building is look for the best echo? The Elks Lodge bathroom is a B-flat. I'm not going to say more. You'll have to come see.

blog.title: THE ELKS LODGE MATINEE: a review of ourselves
blog.body: Attendance: 31. Skanking: 4 at the start, 19 by the third song, and I'll tell you how I know it's 19 because I counted from the second row of the horn line. WITH ALL DUE RESPECT opened. Evan thanked the room twice and apologized for the volume once. (Evan, I love you, but it was 7 minutes of you politely screaming.) Then we played our set, and then something happened. The Elks invited Maple Grove Manor to the matinee, and Grandpa Stan came with his walker with tennis balls on the feet, sat in the second row, and tapped the offbeat the whole show. At the end I said 'we'd like to close with a polka.' Stan sat up. Luis counted it in. We played 'Stan's Polka (Skankin' Version)' and the whole room did the step without knowing they were doing the step. That's it. That's the review. Ska is not dead. It was in the second row. It had tennis balls on its feet.

blog.title: RANKING THE WAVES (a list for beginners)
blog.body: People ask me for a starter pack. Here it is, by wave. FIRST WAVE: Jamaica. The Skatalites. They invented the beat. If you only listen to one record, listen to one of theirs, and then call your grandpa. SECOND WAVE: England. The Specials, Madness, The Selecter. Two-tone. This is where checkerboard came from, and I want you to know I take that personally. THIRD WAVE: America. The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, Less Than Jake, Reel Big Fish, Five Iron Frenzy (Josh, you know), Streetlight Manifesto. The horns got louder and so did the guys holding them. FOURTH WAVE: us. We're local. We're nine. We're the wave that comes in and surprises you at the Elks Lodge. WAVE ZERO: polka. I've been told this isn't a thing. I've decided it is. Ranked by how fast a stranger taps a foot: 1) Skatalites. 2) The Specials. 3) Grandpa Stan. 4) Reel Big Fish. 5) Me, at lunch, no instrument.

blog.title: what my grandpa's trombone case smells like (a love letter)
blog.body: Slide oil. Peppermint. Old Spice. And a thing I can't name that I think is 41 years of weddings. The case has four stickers: the Buckeye Concertina Aces, a Browns helmet, 'I Love Polka' (the heart is a real heart), and a tiny flag. Inside the lid, in marker, in handwriting I'd know anywhere, it says: PLAY IT LIKE YOU MEAN IT, STANLEY. That's me. I'm Stanley the third. Skip since kindergarten, because I skipped everywhere. I found the note the first day I opened the case, when I was twelve, and I haven't cleaned it off, and I never will. When Grandpa gave me the horn he said 'the secret is, there's no secret. You just show up and you blow.' I think that's ska. I think that's the whole thing. I'm going to put it on a T-shirt. (Checkerboard. Obviously.)
